title: A 1984-2015 vapour pressure deficit relation forecast 2016-2024 western US forest fire area with 87% skill, but all nine later years burned more area than predicted (factor 1.56)
abstract: Question: Does the fuel-aridity relation of Abatzoglou and Williams (2016), fitted to western US forest fire area in 1984-2015, forecast later years? Method: We rasterized MTBS fire perimeters (all incidents except prescribed fire) at 240 m and summed burned area in 1/24-degree cells with at least 50% forest in LANDFIRE potential vegetation, west of 103 W. The predictor was standardized March-September PRISM vapour pressure deficit (VPD) over these cells. We fixed an OLS fit of log10 area on 1984-2015 and tested 2016-2024. The pre-specified primary four-metric gridMET index could not be computed because the gridMET server was unavailable; VPD alone was a pre-specified variant. Results: Training r was 0.85. In 2016-2024 the fixed fit reduced squared log error by 87% against the training mean (95% block-bootstrap interval 80-91%), test r was 0.94, and the test-period slope equalled the training slope (0.41 vs 0.42). But all 9 test years burned more than predicted (sign test p = 0.004; mean +0.19 log10, a factor of 1.56; 9.2 Mha observed vs 6.8 Mha predicted); 14 of 16 forested ecoregions had positive offsets. Post hoc, a linear time term fitted on 1984-2015 removed most of the offset; over 1984-2024 it was +0.096 log10 per decade (HAC p about 0.02; block-bootstrap interval -0.004 to 0.167), and it lowered the aridity slope from 0.45 to 0.38. The share of forest burned in the previous 10 years did not reduce later area (no fuel limitation detected). March-June VPD, known on 1 July, gave only 35% skill and was worse than a trend line. Limitations: nine test years, VPD only instead of the paper's eight-metric mean, LANDFIRE BPS instead of ESP, possible MTBS practice changes, and no identification of the cause of the drift. Code, provenance hashes, area series and aggregate results are included; PRISM-derived series are regenerated by script.
